(5) ISSUE #28 (2026-07-20) deleted the `reject` block — 35 terms, all adjudicated NOT-A-PORT-CANDIDATE, none of them backlog and none of them an asserted-absence gold. The terms, verbatim: archetypes = aggro, control, combo, midrange, tempo, aristocrats, voltron, superfriends, pillowfort, group-hug, stax; judgments = value, engine, payoff, inevitability, tech, gas, jank, pile, goodstuff, bomb, haymaker, threat, answer, clock, out, win-con, finisher; social = durdle, brew, netdeck, spike/timmy/johnny, lucksack, whale, misplay. WHY NOT GOLDS (overturning ADR-0004 §7's table row, which said 'becomes asserted-absence golds, one per term'): an asserted-absence gold is `no_arm[P]` over a PORT the engine actually projects (see golds/rat-colony-deck-construction-terminal.json — P0 is the live coarse label emit:anynumberindeck). None of these 35 terms is a port, a stem, an AST discriminator, or a projection of any kind: they are deck-vocabulary, quality and social labels applied by PLAYERS to whole decks, lines of play and each other, not to card text. There is nothing for `SelectArm` to be null over, so `no_arm` is not merely unnecessary here, it is unstatable — and a gold asserting the absence of a port that was never projected would be vacuous in exactly the way ADR-0004 Appendix B's 'the trap this design avoids' describes. WHY NOT BACKLOG: backlog is `projected(corpus) − served − asserted-unarmable` (ADR-0004 §2), and these terms are not in `projected(corpus)` — no card text produces them AS THESE CONCEPTS, so no amount of parser or engine work would ever make one appear. Recording them as backlog would over-report demand that cannot exist. HOMONYM CAVEAT (interaction-judge, 2026-07-20): three spellings collide with live Magic vocabulary — Spike and Whale are CREATURE TYPES (type-ontology.json; Spike Feeder, Killer Whale), and `pile` is a CR 700.3 game term printed on ~32 cards (the Fact or Fiction shape); `value` also occurs inside 'mana value' (CR 202.3) and `control` is CR 110.2. Every one of those collisions is homonymous: what could become a port is a subtype attribute value on an objects:creature port, or a CR 700.3 grouping — a DIFFERENT REFERENT from the psychographic/archetype/judgment label rejected here. The ruling is about the labels, not the spellings. The original $note was already right and needed no conversion: a rejected archetype's MECHANISMS map (an 'aristocrats' deck is emit:removal:creature[manner=sacrificed] → consume:objects:creature plus a drain trigger, all of which ARE ports); the LABEL does not. This is a scope ruling about the taxonomy's vocabulary — architectural, not witnessable — so per ADR-0004 §1 its home is ADR prose (ADR-0004 Appendix C), and this record. kinds.EVENT: discrete occurrences with payloads — what subscriptions (triggered abilities) fire on.
kinds.STATE: pools/stores folded over the event stream (state = fold(events)).
kinds.BEHAVIOR: continuous time-varying values — statics, anthems, keyword grants, 'as long as'.

supergroups.$note: `stems` lists the member stems whose NAME does not already begin with the supergroup's own name — the only membership fact a gold cannot witness (a gold declares a port's stem, never its supergroup). It moved here from the deleted stems_representative[*].supergroup field (#26): membership belongs with the definition it qualifies, and this section is not itself part of a generated artifact. Prefix-named stems (removal:*, deployment:*, modification:*, structure:*) resolve by name and are deliberately NOT listed.

removal.def: a zone-change whose FROM endpoint is play (battlefield/stack): an object leaves play. Carries from/to/manner.

deployment.def: a zone-change whose TO endpoint is play: an object enters play (cast/ETB/token/reanimate/blink-return/copy).

modification.def: an object altered in place: P/T, keyword/ability grant, type/color/control change.

resources.def: fungible pools: mana, cards, life, counters.

objects.def: addressable permanents on the battlefield (F2). Objects = fold(deployment − removal). Bare object-consumes (a sac's fodder decrement) live here; the §10 balance substrate.

structure.def: the clock — a VIEW spanning phase/combat/extra-turn Events and tap/untap availability State (F1: a supergroup may span kinds).

dice-rolled.def: a die roll produces a numeric payload; feeds 'whenever you roll one or more dice' (O19 — dice dissolved, no fourth axis).

damage-dealt.def: damage as an event; edges into resources:life (loss) and, when lethal, removal (state-based death).

combat-presence.def: a permanent attacks or blocks (O21; the attacksorblocks subscription; emit:additionalcombat re-raises the phase that produces it).

connectivity_predictions.$note: falsifiable null hypotheses for the topology sweeps (rollup-vs-scaffold).
connectivity_predictions.P1: every emit:removal:*[manner=sacrificed] (sac outlet) reaches all three consumer rungs — 'when sacrificed', 'when dies' (removal:*[to=graveyard]), 'when leaves battlefield' (removal:*) — by subsumption.
connectivity_predictions.P2: every emit:deployment:creature[token] (token maker) reaches every consume:objects:creature (sac/fodder consumer) via the object store.
connectivity_predictions.P3: color is topology-invariant — it never appears on a stem, only as an attribute; a mono-U and a B/G combo have the same supergroup shape.
connectivity_predictions.P4: irreducible cross-resource bridges (structure:untap → mana) stay AMBER by ceiling.
connectivity_predictions.P5: a self-watching subscription (subject=self) fed by a broad emit ('a creature') tiers AMBER (Overlaps), never GREEN.
connectivity_predictions.P6: every one of the six holes has ≥1 witnessable card in the corpus (else the hole is a taxonomy error, not a coverage gap).
